title: Checks for multiple isinstance calls on the same target.
summary: To check if an object is an instance of any one of multiple types or classes, it is unnecessary to use multiple isinstance calls, as the second argument of the isinstance built-in function accepts a tuple of types and classes. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.212.
message_templates: Multiple `isinstance` calls for `{}`, merge into a single call
Multiple `isinstance` calls for expression, merge into a single call

title: Checks for nested if statements that can be collapsed into a single if statement.
summary: Nesting if statements leads to deeper indentation and makes code harder to read. Instead, combine the conditions into a single if statement with an and operator. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.
message_templates: Use a single `if` statement instead of nested `if` statements

title: Checks for if statements that can be replaced with bool.
summary: if statements that return True for a truthy condition and False for a falsy condition can be replaced with boolean casts. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.214.

title: Checks for try-except-pass blocks that can be replaced with the contextlib.suppress context manager.
summary: Using contextlib.suppress is more concise and directly communicates the intent of the code: to suppress a given exception. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Checks for return statements in try-except and finally blocks.
summary: The return statement in a finally block will always be executed, even if an exception is raised in the try or except block. This can lead to unexpected behavior. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Check for if-else-blocks that can be replaced with a ternary or binary operator.
summary: if-else-blocks that assign a value to a variable in both branches can be expressed more concisely by using a ternary or binary operator. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.213.

title: Checks for boolean expressions that contain multiple equality comparisons to the same value.
summary: To check if an object is equal to any one of multiple values, it's more concise to use the in operator with a tuple of values. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.213.
message_templates: Use `{}` instead of multiple equality comparisons

title: Checks for for loops that can be replaced with a builtin function, like any or all.
summary: Using a builtin function is more concise and readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Check for environment variables that are not capitalized.
summary: By convention, environment variables should be capitalized. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.218.
message_templates: Use capitalized environment variable `{}` instead of `{}`

title: Checks for for loops with explicit loop-index variables that can be replaced with enumerate().
summary: When iterating over a sequence, it's often desirable to keep track of the index of each element alongside the element itself. Prefer the enumerate builtin over manually incrementing a counter variable within the loop, as enumerate is more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Use `enumerate()` for index variable `{}` in `for` loop

title: Checks for if branches with identical arm bodies.
summary: If multiple arms of an if statement have the same body, using or better signals the intent of the statement. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.246.

title: Checks for cases where files are opened (e.g., using the builtin open() function) without using a context manager.
summary: If a file is opened without a context manager, it is not guaranteed that the file will be closed (e.g., if an exception is raised), which can cause resource leaks. The rule detects a wide array of IO calls where context managers could be used, such as open, pathlib.Path(...).open(), tempfile.TemporaryFile() ortarfile.TarFile(...).gzopen(). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.219.
message_templates: Use a context manager for opening files

title: Checks for three or more consecutive if-statements with direct returns.
summary: These can be simplified by using a dictionary Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.250.
message_templates: Use a dictionary instead of consecutive `if` statements

title: Checks for the unnecessary nesting of multiple consecutive context managers.
summary: In Python 3, a single with block can include multiple context managers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.
message_templates: Use a single `with` statement with multiple contexts instead of nested `with` statements

title: Checks for key-existence checks against dict.keys() calls.
summary: When checking for the existence of a key in a given dictionary, using key in dict is more readable and efficient than key in dict.keys(), while having the same semantics. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.176.

title: Checks for negated == operators.
summary: Negated == operators are less readable than != operators. When testing for non-equality, it is more common to use != than ==. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.213.

title: Checks for negated != operators.
summary: Negated != operators are less readable than == operators, as they avoid a double negation. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.213.

title: Checks for double negations (i.e., multiple not operators).
summary: A double negation is redundant and less readable than omitting the not operators entirely. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.213.

title: Checks for if expressions that can be replaced with bool() calls.
summary: if expressions that evaluate to True for a truthy condition an False for a falsey condition can be replaced with bool() calls, which are more concise and readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.214.
message_templates: Use `bool(...)` instead of `True if ... else False`

title: Checks for if expressions that can be replaced by negating a given condition.
summary: if expressions that evaluate to False for a truthy condition and True for a falsey condition can be replaced with not operators, which are more concise and readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.214.
message_templates: Use `not ...` instead of `False if ... else True`

title: Checks for if expressions that check against a negated condition.
summary: if expressions that check against a negated condition are more difficult to read than if expressions that check against the condition directly. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.214.
message_templates: Use `{} if {} else {}` instead of `{} if not {} else {}`

title: Checks for and expressions that include both an expression and its negation.
summary: An and expression that includes both an expression and its negation will always evaluate to False. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Checks for or expressions that include both an expression and its negation.
summary: An or expression that includes both an expression and its negation will always evaluate to True. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Checks for or expressions that contain truthy values.
summary: If the expression is used as a condition, it can be replaced in-full with True. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for and expressions that contain falsey values.
summary: If the expression is used as a condition, it can be replaced in-full with False. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for conditions that position a constant on the left-hand side of the comparison operator, rather than the right-hand side.
summary: These conditions (sometimes referred to as "Yoda conditions") are less readable than conditions that place the variable on the left-hand side of the comparison operator. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.207.

title: Checks for if statements that can be replaced with dict.get calls.
summary: dict.get() calls can be used to replace if statements that assign a value to a variable in both branches, falling back to a default value if the key is not found. When possible, using dict.get is more concise and more idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.219.

title: Checks for static str.split calls that can be replaced with list literals.
summary: List literals are more readable and do not require the overhead of calling str.split. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in 0.10.0.
message_templates: Consider using a list literal instead of `str.{}`

title: Checks for dict.get() calls that pass None as the default value.
summary: None is the default value for dict.get(), so it is redundant to pass it explicitly. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.0.261.

title: Checks for use of zip() to iterate over keys and values of a dictionary at once.
summary: The dict type provides an .items() method which is faster and more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-simplify and made it stable in v0.2.0.
